sections.html:
Hannelore's lyretail, Aphyosemion hanneloreae, is a killifish from Malinga in the Du Chaillu mountains of Ngounié province, southern Gabon. The type locality lies very close to the Republic of the Congo, and the species may also occur across the border.

  • Max size: 40 mm SL (1.6 in SL)

Type locality is Malinga, located in the middle of the Du Chaillu mountain range in Ngounié province, southern Gabon. This lies very close to Republic of the Congo, and the species may also occur across the border.

Aphyosemion: from the Greek aphúe, meaning 'a small fish', and semeion, meaning 'banner, flag', in reference to the "ornamented, often lyre-shaped" caudal fin in male individuals of genus members.

hanneloreae: named for second author Eduard Pürzl's wife, Hannelore Pürzl.
